title: Trust-Region Interior Point Algorithms for a Class of Nonlinear Programming Problems
contribution: Introduces trust-region interior-point (TRIP) reduced SQP algorithms for smooth problems with nonlinear equality (state) constraints and bounds on controls. It proves first- and second-order global convergence, a q-quadratic local rate, and first-order convergence under inexact linear solves with tolerances tied to the trust radius and infeasibility, and tests Fortran 77 code on two PDE optimal control problems (pp. 3-4, 17-18, 165-166).
problem_entry: Enters through an application-defined class (discretized optimal control) whose structure rules out QR factorizations but supplies linearized state/adjoint solvers. The gap is combining that structure with global convergence, bound handling and inexactness, which had been treated only locally or with line searches (pp. 15-17, 88, 137).
key_idea: Compose three proven components (reduced SQP with the nonorthogonal null-space basis W=[-Cy^-1 Cu; I], trust regions as globalizer and regularizer, Coleman-Li affine scaling for bounds) and change only the interacting pieces: a y-only quasi-normal step, a D-scaled tangential subproblem with strict-interiority damping, and decoupled vs coupled trust regions (pp. 16-17, 73-74, 94-97).
assumptions: C2 f and C with bounded derivatives, Cy nonsingular with Cy^-1 uniformly bounded, bounded W_k, H_k, lambda_k and u_k. Tiered step conditions (Cauchy decrease -> first order; optimal decrease + exact Hessian + adjoint multipliers -> second order; take the damped Newton step -> q-quadratic). Nondegeneracy for second-order limits; no state bounds; inexactness only in derivatives of C (pp. 15, 84, 105-107, 135).
proof_devices: contradiction skeleton from Dennis-El-Alem-Maciel: assume ||D_k g_k||+||C_k||>tol, split on ||C_k||<=alpha*delta_k, pred>=kappa*delta_k, penalty bounded, delta_k bounded away from 0, summed ared contradicts bounded merit function (pp. 62-67, 112-115)
Powell's fraction-of-Cauchy-decrease lemma re-proved for a scaled, box-damped Cauchy step (Lemma 2.3.1 p. 28; Lemma 5.3.3 pp. 109-110)
fraction of optimal decrease via the Gay-Sorensen characterization giving pred >= kappa*gamma_k*delta_k^2 for second-order points (pp. 31-32, 101)
ared-pred consistency |ared-pred| <= kappa(||s||^2 + rho(||s||^3 + ||C|| ||s||^2)) (Lemma 3.5.4 p. 59; Lemma 5.3.6 p. 111)
structure makes Ch. 3's extra conditions free: y-only quasi-normal step + adjoint multiplier give grad_x l^T s^q = 0 (Remark 5.2.1, p. 107)
Newton on the nonsmooth scaled system C=0, D^2 W^T grad f=0 with Coleman-Li scaling; |sigma_k-1|=O(||x_k-x*||) damping keeps q-quadratic rate (pp. 90-93, 125-126)
backward-error representation of inexact solves as perturbed operators A_k, B_k with E = e r^T/||r||^2; tolerances O(min{delta_k,||C_k||}) and O(||C_k||) (pp. 136, 139-141, 150-154)
experiments: Two discretized optimal control problems (nonlinear heat boundary control n=2100, m=2000; semilinear elliptic distributed control up to 33282 variables). Internal ablations: decoupled/coupled x reduced/full L-BFGS Hessian, Coleman-Li vs Dikin-Karmarkar scaling (the latter reached a wrong bound), exact vs GMRES inexact solves, mesh refinement. Cost counted in iterations and state/adjoint solves; no external baseline or profiles (pp. 130-134, 157-164).
positioning: Presents itself as simultaneously generalizing Powell/More-Sorensen (unconstrained), Dennis-El-Alem-Maciel/Dennis-Vicente (equality) and Coleman-Li (bounds) via the diagrams of Figs. 1.1-1.2. Surveys TR-SQP around four design questions and critiques QR-based decompositions and unanalysed penalty schemes by reformulation (pp. 19-20, 46-47, 54, 78, 90).
writing: Numbered ingredient and result lists up front (pp. 16-17), a stated contract that each chapter opens with a justified summary (p. 21), tiered Conditions mapped to theorems (pp. 106-107), Remarks separating needed from unneeded conditions (pp. 107, 121), plain scope statements (pp. 87, 135), historical footnotes (pp. 24, 27, 40, 80).
limits_future: Ranked open questions: state bounds first (the multiplier depends on unknown bound multipliers; affine scaling may be the wrong interior-point device), then infinite-dimensional formulation, better step solvers, practical inexactness control (oversolving, local rates), coupled approach under inexactness. The inexact theory is first order only; numerics cover two problems (pp. 136, 166-167).

method_links.note: Fast local step (damped Newton, Condition 5.4) used when inside the trust region and meeting Cauchy decrease, with convergence from the ared/pred ratio test. Newton rather than a heuristic, and a TR ratio rather than sufficient decrease.
Cost counted in expensive oracle calls (state/adjoint solves), but no worst-case complexity: only lim inf stationarity and a local q-quadratic rate (era effect).
Deterministic ancestor: exact solves relaxed to inexact ones with accuracy tied to trust radius and infeasibility (O(min{delta_k,||C_k||}), O(||C_k||)); no probability.

Skeleton reuse strongly evidenced (same merit function, ared/pred, penalty update; proofs follow [35]; inexact proof virtually the same), but the object changed for the new class is the stationarity measure and TR scaling, not the acceptance test.
Solver with switchable design choices used as the ablation and prepared for distribution (F77 + Matlab). Benchmark half is a variant: two applied problems, no collection, baselines or profiles.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: special-case reduction as positioning and correctness check
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: The theorem is stated to reduce to named results for unconstrained, equality- and box-constrained classes, with assumptions reducing to the weakest known ones, and drawn as a contribution map (Figs. 1.1-1.2).

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: design around the user's existing oracle
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: The algorithm needs only linearized state/adjoint solves and matrix-vector products that the application already provides; QR rejected as work of no value except to the optimizer; bounds handled with no extra user information.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: inner accuracy tied to trust radius and infeasibility
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Residuals of state solves O(min{delta_k,||C_k||}), adjoint O(||C_k||), implemented as min{eps, 1e-2 min{||C_k||,delta_k}}. Possible deterministic root of Method 3 and radius-dependent model accuracy (interpretation).
Inexact products and solves rewritten as exact operations with perturbed operators A_k, B_k (rank-one E = e r^T/||r||^2) so the exact convergence proof carries over with bounded perturbations.

transferable: Set inner-solver tolerances from quantities known at iteration start: tol_state = min{eps, 1e-2 min{||C_k||, delta_k}}, tol_adjoint = min{eps, 1e-2 ||C_k||} (pp. 136, 157).

Represent inexact computations as exact ones with rank-one perturbed operators, assume only boundedness and vanishing error on feasible subsequences, then reuse the exact proof (pp. 139-141, 150-154).
Split the step into a feasibility and an optimality component and impose only fraction of Cauchy decrease on each, so any dogleg, CG or GMRES solver fits the theory (pp. 95, 99, 129, 144-149).

Trust-region contradiction skeleton: measure > tol, case split on ||C_k|| vs alpha*delta_k, pred >= kappa*delta_k, bounded penalty, delta_k bounded below, sum of decreases contradicts bounded merit function (pp. 62-67, 112-115).
Contribution-map figure in the introduction showing which prior results on simpler classes the theorem generalizes (pp. 19-20).

When a variant loses, add the diagnostic plot your explanation predicts (distance of the step from the null space of J_k); report a faster alternative that converges to a wrong solution (pp. 133-134, 158-163).
Mesh-refinement table with iterations and counts of expensive solves to support a polynomial-growth claim (p. 164).
coauthors: Single-author thesis (L. N. Vicente); adviser J. E. Dennis; main collaborator M. Heinkenschloss; results shared with Dennis-Heinkenschloss-Vicente [36], Dennis-Vicente [41], [42], Heinkenschloss-Vicente [76], [77].

quotes.text: Thus as the iterates approach feasibility the accuracy with which the linear systems are solved has to increase.
The coupled approach did not perform as well as the decoupled approach. This is explained by the accumulation of errors due to inexactness.
